title: Compile-Time Access Control Bypass via Runtime Inspection
platform_conditions: 'private'/'readonly' exist only in tsc and are erased at emit; ES '#private' fields are enforced by the runtime (V8 and all ES2022 engines)
security_mechanism: The 'private' modifier is a checker-only annotation: tsc emits the field as an ordinary property, so (obj as any).key, JSON round-trips, and Object.entries all read or overwrite it. Class instances rebuilt from payloads lose the invariant the type declared, because deserialization assigns plain fields without running the constructor that established them. '#private' fields are hard slots at the engine level: external code cannot reach them even with any-casts, and deserialization cannot forge them.

source_sink_clues.source: Deserialized objects, any-casts, and reflective access to instances whose internal fields gate security behavior.
source_sink_clues.sink: private/readonly fields holding credentials, roles, or invariants that can be read or rewritten from outside the class

tracking_guards: Check secrets and security invariants use '#private' (or closures/WeakMap) rather than the modifier keyword; check deserialization paths reconstruct instances through validated constructors or static fromJSON factories instead of plain assignment.
not_candidate_when: The private field is non-security and its corruption is contained, the class is never reconstructed from external data, or '#private'is already used for the security-relevant state.
public_references: CWE-668: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/668.html
